preamble: Place assimilation of the moraic nasal to a following velar consonant, yielding the velar nasal [ŋ]. The moraic nasal /N/ (ん) of Japanese is phonologically placeless; [ɴ] is its traditional description in utterance-final position, though real-time MRI work (Maekawa 2023, JIPA 53(1), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100321000050) shows even final /N/ ranges from palatal to uvular closure depending on the preceding vowel. The assimilation itself is regular and exceptionless in Japanese and is shared by Okinawan (Ryukyuan), which has the same moraic nasal; no language outside Japonic is documented with a uvular nasal that assimilates in this way, so the pairing is rare cross-linguistically even though nasal place assimilation in general is very common.

examples.note: /N/ before the velar stop /ɡ/ surfaces as [ŋ].
The moraic nasal before a velar is realized as syllabic [ŋ̍]. In isolation Okinawan /N/ is itself [ŋ̍] rather than uvular.

sources: Okada, H. (1991). Japanese. Journal of the International Phonetic Association, 21(2), 94-96. https://doi.org/10.1017/S002510030000445X
